author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: A hot US labour market (467,000 January payrolls) has forced a front-end repricing - the 2Y at 1.30% after +43 bps over 20 observations, bear flattening on a moderately steep curve - that punishes long-duration growth and rewards energy, banks and capital-return stories, while policy diverges abroad: China eases into a property drag, the ECB pushes back on hike pricing, Poland's NBP tightens into a VAT-cutting tax shield, and the Russia-Ukraine build-up remains a pending two-sided risk carried by oil, gold and defense rather than by European gas.
sources_policy: Only the 2022-02-08 frozen feed (via tools/digest.py, regenerated into a private scratch file) and the 2022-02-08 market card (tools/showcard.py) were used; no other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note, no specs/, retail_drafts/, notes/retail_*, audit/independent_* and no web access. Every number is a card value quoted as shown or a figure in a headline cited in the same part; market figures carry (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-07), Treasury figures (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-07) and crypto (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-07). Company news/previews within seven days, company results within fourteen, macro releases/policy baselines within thirty-five. Previews (24/7 Wall St. on BP/Pfizer, Pekao on the February MPC move, Reuters strategists on $100 oil) are used only as pending events or expectations, never as outcomes; the Nvidia-Arm item is written as a Bloomberg report with formal confirmation pending. No dated calendar claims without a dated headline (the NBP move is 'February' per the Pekao preview; CPI is 'the next print'). No numeric spot-FX; DXY quoted as an index. Period identities used as the card names them: Meta Platforms (FB), Block (SQ), Raytheon Technologies (RTX), Mercedes-Benz Group. No Polish companies in the Sector Deep Dive. Each citation ID is used at most twice (287 distinct IDs, 303 citations). tools/verify.py --nonretail 2022-02-08: PASS, 8,831 body words, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, all per-block ranges in bounds.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n1949 (NYT, 'Nvidia Deal to Buy Arm From SoftBank Is Off After Setbacks', stamped 2022-02-07): states the outcome as fact; the formal termination is an 8 February event and a day-granular US-evening stamp could fall after the cutoff. Only the Bloomberg report n0819 is used, framed as a report with confirmation pending; no Arm IPO plan or SoftBank results are mentioned.
n0771 (Fierce Pharma, Amgen Q4 commentary, stamped 2022-02-07): describes Amgen fourth-quarter results that were released after the US close on 8 February; misdated/after cutoff.

n1221 (Reuters, 'Bank of England raises rates by most since 1995 even as long recession looms', stamped 2022-02-03): contradicts the own-date BoE coverage of a back-to-back rise to 0.5% (n1220, n0518) and appears to describe a later, larger hike; treated as misdated and avoided.
n0016 (RBA, '1 February 2022 | Minutes of the Monetary Policy Meeting'): the stamp reflects the meeting date; the minutes are published later, so the content may postdate the cutoff. Avoided.
n0039 (RBA Statement on Monetary Policy chapter stamped 2022-02-02, before the statement's release): misdated stamp; no SoMP chapter is cited.

n1293 (NYT 'Your Tuesday Briefing: Putin and Macron Meet'): a Tuesday-dated briefing published late Monday US time that may carry post-meeting outcomes; only the meeting itself is used, via n1277 and n1274.

Australian 11:30 AEDT and Chinese 09:30 CST releases on 8 February fall after the cutoff; no 8 February Asian data are referenced. Peloton, Pfizer, BP, Chipotle and SoftBank results and the NBP decision are treated as pending; Peloton's leadership change and results are not mentioned.
n1474 (Asahi, 'BOJ applies minus interest rate for MUFG Bank deposits', monthly category): timing and context unclear; avoided.

n1495 (US troop deployment, source metadata 'U.S. Department of War (.gov)'): source name is anachronistic for the period and cannot be attributed naturally; the same fact is cited from Reuters n1350.

Spot-FX: n1567, n1615, n1616, n1617, n1658 (Business Insider Polska EUR/PLN, USD/PLN, CHF/PLN levels), the 5-groszy figure in n1657, the hypothetical 3.30 zl rate in n1711, n1212 (EUR/USD) and n0931 (exchange-rate roundup) carry numeric currency levels; only direction is used (n1571, n1657 without numbers), and DXY is the only dollar measure quoted.

Promotional or speculative price targets: n0912 (Fundstrat Bitcoin $200k / Ether $12k), n0908 (AVAX to $75), n0616 ('3 hypergrowth stocks that can soar 216% to 257%'), n0757 (Moomoo '50% profit within a day'), n0933 (FTX Super Bowl free-bitcoin promotion), CoinMarketCap and Yahoo quote pages (n0927, n0945, n0946, n0863). Not used.
Super Bowl LVI items (n0096, n0097, n0103, n0106, n0115, n0928 and others): advertising previews only; the game is after the cutoff and no outcome or ad reaction is claimed.
n1695 (Defence24 opinion that there will be no invasion of Ukraine): an opinion forecasting an outcome; avoided. The Russia-Ukraine section treats invasion only as a pending risk.
Card levels withheld (CMCSA, GE, WDC) and the TQQQ older-unit reference are not quoted; TAIEX has no comparable returns and is not used.
